question: Do Colorado counties show stable mobile-test network profiles across sampling, weighting and quarters?
new_technique: Bootstrap-stable unsupervised segmentation with frozen temporal transfer
unit: County summaries of observed Ookla mobile-test tiles, assigned by centroid
transform: Log1p, then standardize using development counties only
selection: Maximum development silhouette subject to each cluster having at least five counties; retain no-segmentation interpretation if silhouette below 0.25
bootstrap: Sample tiles with replacement within each development county; recompute test-weighted summaries and refit scaler and selected K. Compare partitions with ARI and Hungarian-aligned county membership frequency.
baseline: One statewide profile and descriptive county dispersion; K=1 silhouette is undefined
sensitivities: Only tiles with at least five tests
temporal_check: Freeze development scaler and centroids; assign replication-quarter counties without selecting K again. Repeat on matched tiles to diagnose spatial sample turnover.
limits: Tile resampling is conditional on observed tiles; spatial dependence and within-tile uncertainty omitted
Tests are self-selected; device totals are not unique across tiles
County context is ecological and from a different reference year
No carrier identity or subscriber denominator
Profiles are descriptive, not a causal or production segmentation
